title: TCP: Implement 2 new fields to track who sent TCP RST first: client or server.
description:
A fair bit of networking issues troubleshooting involves figuring out
who sent TCP RST first.
And quite often some middlebox/firewall/router sends TCP RST to both
parties.
To simplify troubleshooting let's add two filters
tcp.connection.rst_client and tcp.connection.rst_server

I can tell just by looking at the code that it won't work 100% of the time. The only time packets are guaranteed to be dissected in order is the first pass.  The second (and subsequent passes based on when a user clicks on or scrolls to a packet) will cause redissection which can reset your conversation variables in an undesirable way. You'll probably have to cache the determined closing RST with something like p_set_proto_data/p_get_proto_data and PINFO_FD_VISITED

Apologies for the delay.
Thank you for your latest commit, it helped me understand that code much better, but it didn't work with some of my pcaps.
It is my bad, I should have explained better what I am trying to do:
1. for every tcp conversation with rst, there should either be tcp.connection.rst_client or tcp.connection.rst_server, but not both, because we don't really care about tcp rst sent in response to original tcp rst
2. and none should be set when we saw fin before rst, because we don't care about rst in response to fin

So, this filter, combined with other filters (frame.time and/or tcp completeness and others) will allow me to identify the faulting party in the tcp stream: who sent tcp rst first, before fin

I have pushed the latest commit, please let me know your thoughts, thank you for the review!

That looks OK to me.
There shouldn't be any RST answer to an RST as it can end in an infinite loop, but things happen.
